memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and a thick and dreadful darkness came over him. - Gen 15:12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The sun goes down, Abram falls into a deep sleep, and "a thick and dreadful darkness came over him." What a strange moment to place right in the middle of a covenant ceremony. God is about to make His most solemn promise - and first comes dread and darkness.

Scripture is being honest with us. Encountering the living God is not always a warm, comfortable experience. He is holy, and holiness is weighty. When people in the Bible truly meet God, they often fall down, tremble, or are struck with awe. Isaiah cried, "Woe to me! I am ruined!" (Isa 6:5). God is good, but He is not tame.

Notice also that Abram is asleep - completely passive. He contributes nothing to what is about to happen. He cannot even watch. The covenant that follows will be entirely God's doing, and Abram is unconscious for it.

That is not incidental; it is the whole point. Our salvation does not rest on our alertness, our effort, or our contribution. It rests on God alone. If you are in a dark, dreadful season, it does not mean God has abandoned His promise. Sometimes the darkness is exactly where God does His deepest covenant work - while we can do nothing but rest.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you assumed darkness means God is absent?
- Can you rest in a covenant that depends entirely on God, not you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You are holy and Your presence is weighty. When darkness comes, help me remember You are still keeping Your promises. Thank You that my salvation rests on Your work, not mine.
Amen.
